newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- China will invest 30 billion yuan to improve the environment along the Huai River and Taihu Lake, which are major agricultural production areas in central and eastern China.
- China Central Television Station will for 72 hours from the morning of June 30 to July 3 air programmes on the various activities held to celebrate the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- China earned $2.56 billion from overseas tourists in the first three months of 1997.
- The Henan Provincial Supreme People's Court will hear China's first dispute involving greenbean futures trading.
CHINA SECURITIES
- The China Securities Regulatory Commission sets up a telephone hotline for people to report on securities irregularities.
- The Ministry of Construction issues rules on urban property mortgages.
- A report by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences says China's toy, textile and shoe industries should restructure and boost technology to better compete in the international market.
- The Industrial and Commercial Bank of China says it lost 23.88 billion yuan in 1995-96 due to bankruptcies of firms.
ECONOMIC DAILY
- China's state firms covered under the government budget made profits of 2.57 billion yuan in January-April this year, a drop of 32.9 percent from the year-ago period.
Total losses of loss-making state firms hit 25.78 billion yuan in the period, up a year-on-year 2.1 percent.
BEIJING ECONOMIC DAILY
- The Beijing Meter and Machine Tool Factory wins a 27.58 million yuan contract to help build a subway project in Iran.
CHINA BUSINESS TIMES
- Wuhan Iron and Steel Co has set up non-steel firms to employ 70,000 workers laid off from its steel factories.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH

- Premier Li Peng says China has always viewed its friendly cooperation with African countries as an important part of its foreign policy and sees this cooperation as increasingly important at the turn of the century.
CHINA DAILY

- Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang urges Japan not to creat any new problems for bilateral relations, saying Tokyo should take effective measures to stop rightists from invading the Diaoyu Islands.
